beats.says: Nodes 0, 1 and 2 are the acceptors. Two matchmakers keep which acceptors each ballot uses. Node 3 waits outside.
To lead, node 0 first registers ballot 2.0 with acceptors 0, 1 and 2 at the matchmakers.
Only now does node 0 send its Prepare. Two promises of three: node 0 leads.
A client writes alpha. Two votes of three choose it at slot 0.
Now node 2 must leave, and node 3 takes its place.
A set never changes in place. Node 0 registers a new ballot, 3.0, with acceptors 0, 1 and 3.
Phase 1 runs again, and node 0 leads at ballot 3.0 with acceptors 0, 1 and 3.
The new set chooses bravo at slot 1.
The log grows for ever. So the leader can cut it into segments, each a range of slots.
A client asks node 0 to roll. The Roll is a command: node 0 proposes it at slot 2, like a write.
Node 0 does not wait for the Roll. It proposes charlie at slot 3 at once.
Both are chosen. Each node applies the Roll at slot 2: segment 0 ends there, and segment 1 starts at slot 3.
Paxos chose one value at slot 2, so every node ends segment 0 at the same slot.
Now node 0 crashes.
Node 1 registers ballot 4.1. The matchmakers report two sets: 0, 1, 2 for ballot 2.0 and 0, 1, 3 for ballot 3.0.
Phase 1 needs a majority of each set. Node 2 is not in the new set, but its promise still counts for the old one.
Node 1 takes its segment from its own chosen log: segment 1, from slot 3.
Node 1 rolls again, at slot 4. Segment 1 ends there, and segment 2 starts at slot 5.
Node 1 beats. Its ballot holds, so the matchmakers forget the sets below it.
No set names node 2 now, so it retires.
A new set is a new ballot, and a cut is a command of the log.
